summary: Docs 10 KB 4: log-only hook warning on oversize linked docs
author: pm
body:
Candidate project hook (log-only): after a write to `.claude/docs/**.md`, log when the file is over 10 KB. Needs the hook framework and the review phase (global rules).

**Done when:** hook built log-only, reviewed and installed, or ruled not worth it.

Source: user request 2026-11-23 (d-026); .claude/docs/documentation.md.

**Installed, 2026-11-24:** rule D1 is installed in `.claude/hooks/` and wired in the new `.claude/settings.json` as PostToolUse on Write|Edit|MultiEdit. It is log-only, logging to `.claude/hooks/log/doc_size_hits.jsonl` (gitignored). The read-only review passed twice (fixes in between). The live self-test passes 35/35 (measured). A live smoke test with an 11,229 B throwaway doc in `.claude/docs/` logged one row (`would_flag: true`); the doc was then deleted. The replay found 11 hits and 0 false positives. d-030 was classified not hookable (judgment). `documentation.md`'s size check is aligned to 10,240 B.

**Needs the user (user_review):** (1) should D1 show its message to the agent (`--flag`) instead of only logging? (2) Should an assessed (kept-whole) doc re-flag each time it grows past another 2 KB? (3) Should the hook become global (it is generalized; global hooks need the user's approval)?

comments.author: pm
comments.body: 2026-11-24 triage: stays in user_review. The hook is built, reviewed, installed and self-tested (35/35); what is left are three policy choices only the user can make: (1) show D1's message to the agent (--flag) instead of log-only? (2) re-flag a kept-whole doc each time it grows another 2 KB? (3) make the hook global (global hooks need your approval)?
